head: c3cc860edeb2bf5bfcfa580eded00e39f0a98718
summary:
The product change is what the design asked for, and it is correct. `ShellReveal.Walk` now parses the target once, opens it once and frees it once. It refuses on any failure of the parse or the open: 0x80070002 and 0x80070003 become NoLongerExists, and any other code is passed through as is. Nothing falls back to an ancestor any more. `RevealKind.Ancestor` is gone, and the settled Fitness rule stops it coming back. `FormatRevealStatus` and `RevealFailure` produce the designed texts. I checked the FACILITY_WIN32 mask arithmetic, where int & uint widens to long, and it gives the right result.

What I ran:
- Full default suite: 496 passed, 0 failed.
- App build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Hook build (outside the solution): 0 warnings.
- WindowCases.ps1: parses with 0 errors.
- rules-parity: AGREE.
- Fitness op=check: all 69 rules hold.
- No reference to Ancestor survives in src or in tests/window.

Every departure from the design is declared.

The tests feed the shapes:
- The real-tree STA unit test does delete the parent and the leaf. It uses a present file and a FILE_ALL_ACCESS deny folder as controls that must reach the open.
- SelectSwitchRuleTests reads the rule's own pattern from the Fact source.
- R-002 builds exactly the fixtures the matrix names:
  - a FullControl deny on the short folder and on the 300-character folder, each checked unlistable before the scan;
  - files of exactly 161, 300 and 1000 characters;
  - a pre-opened parent with the sibling selected;
  - a deleted parent opened through the gate.

Steps a–d of R-002 and all of R-001 have never been run by any stage. So whether the landing, the 1 s bound and SC-007's existing cases actually hold is still unknown until validate or a person runs them.

One defect is in the new window-test helpers. Compare-ExplorerState matches Explorer windows by HWND and compares only the first entry for each HWND. In Windows 11, every tab of a tabbed Explorer window has the same HWND in Shell.Application (that part is from my own knowledge; I did not test it here). If so, an Explorer window with two or more tabs that nobody touches is reported as 'moved'. That fails R-002 step (e) and R-001's dup. step with no cause. I showed the comparison logic does this by feeding it a synthetic state.

Second round: This second pass went back over every parser and matcher the diff adds or rewires, looking for inputs it does not expect:
- ShellReveal.Plan / IsMisparsed
- Walk's HRESULT handling
- RevealFailure's facility mask
- FactPatterns, which reads the Fact source (checked against CRLF and the new Fact's layout)
- the yaml entry
- WindowCases' LongPath (null, empty, "::", UNC, \\?\, trailing backslash)
- Find-Landing (empty or virtual item paths)
- Get-ExactPath's arithmetic
- the R-002 marker reader
- -Step validation, which is case-insensitive and still works
- the hook gate's error paths

One new defect, measured rather than argued. I ran a parse-only probe that opens no window: SHParseDisplayName with a SHGetPathFromIDListEx round-trip, on Windows 11 26200:
- `con.txt`, `nul.log`, `com1.txt` and `aux.h` each parse with hr=0 and round-trip exactly to themselves.
- A bare `con` gives 0x800704B0.
- `dup.` parses to the decoy `dup`.

So these items are addressable, and a reveal would land on them. SL-088's Plan refuses them anyway without asking the shell, and shows the person a false reason. Everything else from round 1 stands: m1 on HWND-keyed window comparison, and cases a–d of R-002 plus R-001 never having been run.

findings.claim: Compare-ExplorerState matches the before and after states by Hwnd alone and compares only `$old[0]`. When two Shell.Application entries share an HWND, which is how Windows 11 lists the tabs of one tabbed Explorer window, an unchanged state is reported as 'the Explorer window on A moved to B'. The consequence: R-002 step (e), the only window test for criterion 6, and R-001 step 3 (dup.) Watch-ExplorerUnchanged both fail with no cause whenever the person has any tabbed Explorer window with 2+ tabs open. Validate runs these on the person's desktop, so that can send the slice round a loop for nothing. It never produces a false pass. The same keying in Close-CaseWindows has a second effect: a case window that Explorer opens as a new tab in a window already in the baseline is never closed and never counted. The isolation check then passes with that tab still open, and the tab is left behind on a deleted fixture folder.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Compare-ExplorerState: `$old = @($before.Windows | Where-Object Hwnd -eq $w.Hwnd)` … `elseif ($old[0].Folder -ne $w.Folder)`. Close-CaseWindows: `if ($w.Hwnd -in $baselineHwnds -or ...) { continue }`. Reproduced by loading the real functions from the script's AST and comparing a state that has two entries on Hwnd 100 (C:\A, C:\B) with itself. The result was 1 change: "the Explorer window on 'C:\A' moved to 'C:\B'". This machine currently has 1 Explorer entry, so the shared-HWND premise itself could not be observed here.
findings.fix: In Compare-ExplorerState, stop keying on Hwnd alone. Reduce each entry to a string `"$Hwnd|$Folder|$Selected"` and report every after-entry whose string is not among the before-entries. New visible Cabinets stay as they are. In Close-CaseWindows, drop the baseline-HWND test for entries whose resolved folder is under the case roots. Those roots are fresh GUID folders that nothing else can have open, and Test-Under alone already protects the person's own windows.

findings.claim: IsMisparsed checks for reserved names on the part of the name before the first dot, so `con.txt`, `nul.log`, `aux.h` and `com1.txt` all count as unaddressable. Since SL-088, Plan returns `RevealPlan(null, badName, display)` for those names, and Walk refuses them without asking the shell. The status line then says "Couldn't show 'aux.h' in Explorer (Explorer can't select 'aux.h' by name: it ends in a dot or space, or is a reserved device name). Nothing was opened." The same refusal covers every item below a folder with such a name. On this machine the shell addresses every one of these names exactly, so the reveal would have landed and the reason shown is false. The build's declared deviation assumes these names are mis-parsed, and that holds only for trailing-dot or trailing-space names (`dup.` goes to `dup`) and for bare device names. The test `Plan_UnaddressableNames_RecordTheNameAndAskTheShellForNothing` pins the wrong answer with `[InlineData(@"C:\con.txt", "con.txt")]`.
findings.evidence:
src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/ShellReveal.cs:124-126 (Plan returns early on IsMisparsed) and :138-150 (`baseName = component[..dot]` compared with CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/CONIN$/CONOUT$, with COMn/LPTn at :152-164). tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ShellRevealTests.cs:26. Parse-only probe in %TEMP%, files created through \\?\ paths, cleaned up afterwards:
- con.txt: hr=0, back=<dir>\con.txt
- nul.log: hr=0, back=<dir>\nul.log
- com1.txt: hr=0, back=<dir>\com1.txt
- aux.h: hr=0, back=<dir>\aux.h
- con: hr=0x800704B0
- dup.: hr=0, back=<dir>\dup
The selection in a real Explorer window was not observed. The round-trip PIDL is the target itself.
findings.fix: In IsMisparsed, compare the reserved-name list against the whole component with trailing spaces trimmed, not against the text before the first dot. That keeps trailing-dot and trailing-space names and bare `con` or `com1` refused, and lets `con.txt` reach SHParseDisplayName, whose HRESULT already refuses anything the shell cannot address. Move `C:\con.txt` from the unaddressable theory to Plan_UnusualAddressableNames_StaysExact. Windows 10's parse of `con.txt` was not measured here. If it parses to something other than the file, keep the extension form refused on Windows 10 only.

obligations.evidence:
The test exists but has never run. tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-R002 step 'a':
- Deny-All adds a FullControl Deny FileSystemAccessRule on the \\?\ form. .NET keeps the full mask for a FullControl deny.
- Test-Listable is asserted false before the scan.
- It reveals `tree:denyall_short`, requires Check-Landing plus a Name check, and watches for #32770 dialogs and consent.exe.
The Core side is shown: Walk_OnRealTree includes a FILE_ALL_ACCESS deny folder that parses and reaches the open. The Explorer landing is unknown because steps a–d were never run by any stage.

Test-R002 step 'b': Get-ExactPath gives a path of exactly 161 characters (CheckEqual), revealed from `largest:`. The step is timed with $timed=$true against the hook's revealStartQpc. It is written and has not run.

Test-R002 step 'b', second iteration: a file of exactly 300 characters, revealed from its `largest:` row. It needs exactly one selected item and uses Resolve-LongPath on both sides. R-001 step 10 is also padded to exactly 300 characters (CheckEqual 300). Neither has run.
Test-R002 step 'd': the 1000-character file is created through .NET long-path calls, CheckEqual 1000, and revealed from its `largest:` row within 1000 ms. It has not run.

Test-R002 step 'c': a Deny-All folder of exactly 300 characters (CheckEqual 300), verified unlistable, revealed from its `tree:` row. It is timed, gets a Name check and has the dialog watch. Its target is distinct from step (b)'s. It has not run.

Test-R002's `$steps = 'b','a','c','d','e'` makes the 161-character reveal the first one of a `-Case R-002` run, with no warm-up and with $timed=$true. It is unrun. Under `-Case All`, R-001's reveals come before it.

Test-R002 step 'd':
- `[FsaWindowCases.Win32]::Reveal($sibling)` opens the parent, then Wait-ExplorerSelection requires the sibling as the only selection before the click.
- Find-Landing looks at every window and needs Selected.Count -eq 1 with that item equal to the target.
It has not run.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ShellRevealTests.cs Walk_OnRealTree_RefusesGoneTargetsAndLandsThePresentOne:
- It deletes gone\ and runs the real SHParseDisplayName on an STA thread.
- It asserts Failed/NoLongerExists and no open call, that tree.Root parses S_OK, and that exactly 2 opens came from the controls.
- It passed in my run of the full suite (496/496).
Window side: Test-R002 step 'e' uses FSA_HOOK_REVEAL_GATE (hook RevealMode.WaitAtGate) and Compare-ExplorerState. The builder recorded a pass through the published exe.

The same real-tree test deletes kept\deleted.bin while kept\ remains, and asserts NoLongerExists with no open. The Walk_TargetNoLongerExists_RefusesWithoutOpeningAnything theory covers 0x80070002 and 0x80070003 and asserts Opened and Freed are empty. Both pass.

Walk_OpenFails_RefusesWithItsCodeFreesTheIdListAndTriesNothingElse: the fake parse returns S_OK and the fake open returns E_FAIL. It asserts one parse, one open and one free of the same PIDL, Failed with E_FAIL, and Shown null. ShellReveal.cs:214-222 frees the PIDL in a finally. The test passes.

Walk_ParseFailsOtherwise_RefusesWithThatCode feeds 0x80070005, 0x8007007B, 0x80070035 and 0x80004005. Each gives Failed with that HRESULT, Reason None and no open. ShellReveal.cs:208-212 only maps 2 and 3 to NoLongerExists. The test passes.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/SelectSwitchRuleTests.cs reads the pattern from ArchitectureRulesTests.NothingInTheAppHandsExplorerItsSelectSwitch through FactPatterns, then asserts that ArgumentList.Add("/select"), "/SELECT,", "/select \"", "/select," and the interpolated form all match. The twinned yaml entry is `(?m)/[Ss][Ee][Ll][Ee][Cc][Tt]\b` with including_comments: true. rules-parity reports AGREE, and Fitness op=check reports 69 rules holding.
SelectSwitchRuleTests.TheRuleLeavesLookAlikesAlone asserts no match on "/selection", "selected" and "Open in Explorer". Plants P25-P27 in eng/rules-harness/plants.json cover the same. It passes.

cases.evidence: R-002 step (a) in WindowCases.ps1 feeds the shape: a FullControl Deny ACE applied through the .NET ACL API, checked unlistable with Test-Listable before the scan, revealed from its tree row, with a Name check and a dialog/consent watch. It has never been run.
R-002 step (b): Get-ExactPath at 161 characters, asserted with CheckEqual, revealed from a biggest-files row and timed. It has never been run.
R-002 step (b): exactly 300 characters, revealed with `largest:<leaf>`. Find-Landing resolves 8.3 aliases through GetLongPathNameW on the \\?\ form. It has never been run.
R-002 step (d): exactly 1000 characters, created through .NET long-path calls, revealed from its `largest:` row and timed. It has never been run.
R-002 step (c): a Deny-All folder of exactly 300 characters, verified unlistable, revealed with `tree:<leaf>`. Its target is distinct from step (b)'s file. It has never been run.

R-002 runs its steps in the order b, a, c, d, e, so in a `-Case R-002` run the 161-character reveal comes first, is timed, and has no warm-up. Under `-Case All`, R-001's reveals come first, so this shape is fed only when R-002 runs by itself. It has never been run.
R-002 step (d) pre-opens the parent with only the sibling selected through Win32::Reveal, checks that state, then reveals the target. Find-Landing needs Selected.Count -eq 1. It has never been run.

ShellRevealTests.Walk_OnRealTree deletes gone\ and runs the real parse on an STA thread, with controls that must reach the open. R-002 step (e) deletes gone\ after the scan through the hook gate. The unit test passed in my run; the builder recorded step (e) passing.
Walk_OnRealTree deletes kept\deleted.bin while kept\ survives, and the real parse gives not-found. The fake-shell theory covers 0x80070002 and 0x80070003.
Walk_OpenFails_RefusesWithItsCodeFreesTheIdListAndTriesNothingElse: the fake parse returns S_OK and the fake open returns E_FAIL.
Walk_ParseFailsOtherwise_RefusesWithThatCode is an InlineData theory over 0x80070005, 0x8007007B, 0x80070035 and 0x80004005.

SelectSwitchRuleTests.TheRuleCatchesEveryWayOfHandingExplorerTheSwitch applies the Fact's own pattern, read from its source, to ArgumentList.Add("/select"), "/SELECT," and "/select \"". It also pins that SL-047's pattern misses these three.
SelectSwitchRuleTests.TheRuleLeavesLookAlikesAlone: "/selection", "selected" and "Open in Explorer" do not match.

This case is deferred by the design and is not material. R-001 step 5 feeds a Hidden+System file but asserts only the kind (Exact) and the hidden note, not the Explorer selection. The deferral reason still holds: the reveal-selects-hidden-and-system-items spike is still waiting on a person, and ShellReveal still reports Exact from hr==0 for such items.

drift: No undeclared departure of consequence. Each difference from the design matches one of the build's declared deviations: TryReveal folded into the delegate-based Walk, Walk made internal, RevealPlan.Candidates replaced by Target, unaddressable names refused, step order b,a,c,d,e, the FSA_HOOK_REVEAL_GATE seam, the explicit-class regex, the -Step parameter, and the settled copy of the select-switch rule replaced by the twinned entry.
One small addition goes beyond the design's hook-record contract: the hook's reveal line also carries `qpcFrequency`, which Check-Landing needs to turn QPC ticks into milliseconds.

Get-ExactPath's middle folder names are 60 characters, but the last folder and the leaf are split from what is left and can be shorter than the 50-69 characters the design gave for components. Every total length is still exact.

The build's declared deviation says names the shell mis-parses ('dup.', 'con', 'dir.\in.txt') are refused. In the code, the reserved-name check also covers names with an extension ('con.txt', 'aux.h'), and those the shell addresses exactly on this machine (m2). What the deviation claims and what the code does differ for that subset.
